documents.title: Emergency Department Record (received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, date of service 3/13/2026.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Chief concern: sister reports patient has not slept in three days and is acting unlike herself.

HPI: 29F with a hypomanic episode requiring admission here about a year ago presents with her sister for the same picture. Loud, fast speech; she is pulled off topic by noise in the hallway. Describes herself as able to do things others cannot. Has run up large online purchases, which her sister says is not like her. Patient denies any recent stressor, drug or alcohol use, or physical illness. Per sister, there have been two comparable spells in the last five years, each about a week long, each followed by a period of severe depression.

Meds: none. PSH: wisdom teeth age 18. FH: mother bipolar I, paternal grandfather MDD. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: VS within normal limits. No stigmata of drug use, not intoxicated. Mood euphoric, affect labile. Remainder of exam normal.

Data: CBC normal. Electrolytes normal. TSH and free T4 normal. Urine toxicology screen negative.

Impression: recurrent hypomanic episode. Psychiatry consulted; admit to inpatient psychiatric unit.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Inpatient Psychiatry Discharge Summary (received)
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient psychiatric unit.
Admitted 3/13/2026 from the ED. Discharged 3/20/2026.
Allergies: NKDA.

Reason for admission: second hypomanic presentation in roughly a year, three days without sleep, grandiosity and impulsive spending, brought by family.

Hospital course: Admitted voluntarily. Started on quetiapine at night and titrated to 100 mg at bedtime, tolerated with some morning sedation. Sleep normalized by day 4. Speech and goal-directed activity returned to baseline. Collateral from sister describes two prior elevated spells over five years with depressive stretches afterward. No suicidal ideation at any point. No substance use.

Discharge diagnosis: bipolar II disorder, most recent episode hypomanic.

Discharge medication: quetiapine 100 mg by mouth at bedtime.

Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry intake 4/8/2026 (arranged). PCP follow-up within 1 to 2 weeks.

Condition at discharge: stable, future-oriented, denies SI/HI.

documents.title: External fill history
documents.author: MA
documents.body: External Rx history flag: quetiapine 100 mg #30 filled 3/20/26, prescriber is a hospital psychiatrist. No hospital notification on file. Routed to RN to reach out.

documents.title: Outreach after new prescription
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt about new quetiapine fill. She confirms she was admitted to the psych unit 3/13 to 3/20 and went home on quetiapine nightly. Taking it. Groggy in the morning, otherwise okay. Denies SI. Sister staying with her this week. Scheduled with PCP Wed 3/25. Records request sent to hospital.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wendy comes in with her sister after her second psychiatric admission, 3/13 to 3/20. Hospital paperwork not received; we learned of the stay from the pharmacy fill. History from both of them.

About three days with no sleep, fast talking, big online purchases, feeling she could do anything. Same picture as last March. Her sister adds that there were two similar spells in the last five years, each about a week, each followed by weeks of deep depression; one was before Wendy joined us, and neither low stretch was ever brought to a doctor. The inpatient team told her the diagnosis is bipolar II disorder and started quetiapine 100 mg at bedtime. Psychiatry intake is set for 4/8.

Taking quetiapine every night. Sleeping 9 hours, slow to get going in the morning. Denies SI. No alcohol or drugs.

PHQ-9 5.

Exam: Vitals normal. Tired-appearing, calm, normal speech rate, linear and goal directed. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Bipolar II disorder, recent hypomanic episode with admission. Quetiapine 100 mg qhs per hospital; psychiatry to manage. Added to our list.
2. Medication counseling: discussed sedation, weight and metabolic effects; will check A1c and lipids in about two months. Talked about pregnancy planning and contraception while on psychiatric medication; she is not planning a pregnancy and will raise it with psychiatry before any change.
3. Records request re-sent to the hospital.
Follow up after the psychiatry intake, about 6 to 8 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Psychiatric diagnostic evaluation with medical services

documents.title: Psychiatry intake letter (received)
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient psychiatry, community mental health group. Seen 4/8/2026.

Dear colleague,
Thank you for sharing the care of Ms. McGrath, 29, seen for intake after her March inpatient stay. She has bipolar II disorder with two documented hypomanic episodes needing admission (2025 and 2026) and, by family report, earlier elevated and depressive spells. Mother has bipolar I.

Since discharge she reports steady mood and good sleep on quetiapine 100 mg nightly. Morning fog is easing. No depressive symptoms now. No SI. No substances. Allergies: none known.

Mental status: well related, normal speech, euthymic, full affect, linear, no psychosis, good insight.

Plan: continue quetiapine 100 mg at bedtime. Psychotherapy referral within our group. Please obtain baseline metabolic labs (A1c, lipid panel) and weight; we will follow them with you. Return here in about three months.

Outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: Labs at your May visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy, I got your psychiatrist's letter, and the hospital records finally came too. At your May 13 visit we'll draw the blood work they asked for (sugar and cholesterol). Nothing to fast for, but morning is easiest.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Follow-up for bipolar II on quetiapine 100 mg at night, now about 8 weeks in. Saw psychiatry 4/8, next visit there in July. Mood even. Sleeping 7 to 8 hours. Still a little groggy for the first hour of the day, manageable with coffee. Back at work full time. No racing thoughts, no spending sprees, no low mood. No SI. Taking it nightly.

PHQ-9 3.

O: Weight unchanged from March. BP and pulse normal. Bright, relaxed, normal speech. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no tremor.

A/P:
1. Bipolar II disorder, stable on quetiapine. Continue; psychiatry manages dosing.
2. Metabolic monitoring on an antipsychotic: A1c, lipid panel and CMP drawn today, weight recorded. Will send results to psychiatry.
3. Due for physical in the fall, flu then.
RTC fall.

documents.title: Your results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news: your A1c, cholesterol, liver and kidney tests are all in the normal range. I faxed a copy to your psychiatrist.

documents.title: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: My pharmacy says my quetiapine needs a new prescription. Can you send it or does it have to be the psychiatrist?

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Wendy, since your psychiatrist manages that medication, please call their office for the refill. If they can't get to it before you run out, let us know and we'll bridge you.

documents.title: RE: Refill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Called them, they sent it. Thanks.

documents.title: Psychiatry follow-up letter (received)
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient psychiatry follow-up, 7/15/2026.

Ms. McGrath remains euthymic on quetiapine 100 mg at bedtime. No hypomanic or depressive symptoms since discharge. Sleep regular. Mild morning sedation, tolerable. Metabolic labs from your office in May reviewed, normal. Engaged in therapy.

Plan: no change; continue quetiapine 100 mg at bedtime. Return in three months.

Outpatient psychiatry

documents.title: Scheduling
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Can I book a check-in for late September? Mornings are best.
